quotes.text: Though the Lord had indeed been Abram's "shield" in the rescue of Lot and others and now reminded him of an "exceeding great reward" for his obedience (Gen. 15:1; Abr. 2:6), Abram was growing old and understandably felt that no other reward would be of lasting significance unless he received fulfillment of the promise of seed (Gen. 12:2; 13:16; Abr. 2:9-11). That seed would become the "great nation" and bless all families of the whole earth.

Heavenly fire has often been used by the Lord in giving miraculous manifestations to his prophets. (Gen. 15:17; Ex. 3:2; 24:17; 1 Ne. 1:6.) Lehi and Nephi, sons of Helaman, "were encircled about as if by fire, . . . and were not burned," as a means of protecting them in their ministry, a miracle soon expanded to embrace "about three hundred souls." (Hela. 5:23-49.) Fire from heaven encircled groups of worshipers in connection with the ministry of the resurrected Lord among the Nephites (2 Ne. 17:23-24; 19:13-14), and the Three Nephite disciples were cast into fiery furnaces and came out unharmed. (3 Ne. 28:21; 4 Ne. 32; Morm. 8: 24.) Similar protection was given Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego when Nebuchadnezzar had them cast into a fiery furnace so hot that it slew the handlers who carried out the deed. (Dan. 3.)

First, remember that the RLDS church rejects this section of the D&C [132]. Therefore, when you reject this section, you reject verses 29-33. It is the only place in all scripture where the Abrahamic Covenant is explained. You will never figure it out unless you read those verses. Here the Lord explains it to Abraham, in the context of a revelation on Marriage. That is why it always shows up in the context of Marriage; Jacob, Isaac, etc. They are worried about who they are going to marry, because it directly influences the covenant. Notice that Abraham has a promise that he can continue to be a father and have children both in time and eternity. The patriarchs keep getting two types of blessings, which the world only sees one half. They see the blessing for all generations of time, but don't see that for eternity. The world can't see the eternal blessings. But the Lord sees it for all eternity. That is what made Abraham different from all the others around him. The ultimate revelation is that God is God and glorifies himself by having children throughout all eternity. This is the law by which God glorifies himself. He is our Father. Abraham will become like him because he has the same covenant that made God our Father. You can't find that anywhere else. It is only in the D&C. Notice in the Old Testament the name change. Abram, to Abraham. Exalted Father to Exalted Father of Nations. He has become like God, the Father. What about the other half of the covenant, the LAND? Where is the seed supposed to live forever? Cryptic language for the earth becoming the Celestial Kingdom. D&C 88:17-20. That is where God tells us that the earth will become the Celestial Kingdom, and that is when the meek and the poor of the earth inherit it. Note that Moses takes the Children of Israel into the Promised Land. The Promised Land is a small model of the Celestial Kingdom. Therefore it is important to keep the covenant on the land, because it is supposed to stay pristine and pure...for it represents the Celestial Kingdom. If they break the covenants they make with God, they will be cut off from the land. It will "separate" them. And they make the covenant by cutting the carcass, and the blood on the ground. The curse of the law of Moses, is that if you break the covenant and don't live the law of the land, which is the law of God, the land itself will "vomit you out and your carcasses will lie on the ground." Harsh covenant language, because you are polluting a model of the Celestial Kingdom. When you break the covenant and pollute the Celestial type, your carcass will have to lay on the ground. That was your deal with God. "May God do to me this and more so, if I do not keep my covenant." Then the land becomes called DESOLATE. Here's how you know that the Book of Mormon is an ancient document. No twentieth century farm boy will figure this out. When the city of Ammonihah was run over by Lamanites, after Alma prophesied that it would be, what happened? The "carcasses" were described on the ground, the fowls came and plucked the flesh, and the Nephites called it the Desolation of Nehors. There it is. The covenant curse. Mormon is trying to show that the law is still intact, and they broke the covenant. When they got the Jaredite records and found out that both groups had killed each other off, and rejected the prophets, they named the whole land northward the land of Desolation. They found carcasses (bones) on the ground. Law of Moses.
